Actual expansion of one cleared generic theta section gives f*d_y tending to zero. Artin-Rees for the single finite submodule fR cancels this one denominator uniformly in the index, without claiming a uniform arithmetic constant.
Krull intersection for the finite stalk quotient L/fL proves regularity at every closed-fibre point. No nonproper formal algebraization theorem is presumed.

Flat going-down puts every vertical codimension-one point over a height-one prime; the geometrically integral fibre gives its unique divisor, whose closure contains the closed fibre. Generic regularity handles horizontal poles, and normality removes all poles.
